entities.name: Battle of Neretva
entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The Battle of Neretva was a pivotal event in World War II, marking the final phase of the Axis Operation Weiss and the Partisan counter-offensive in Herzegovina. On February 1, 1943, the battle commenced, pitting the Axis forces against the Yugoslav Partisans, led by Josip Broz Tito. The battle raged on for nearly two months, concluding on April 1, 1943. 

 The clash was a testament to the determination and resilience of the Partisan forces, who successfully held off the Axis advance. The battle also showcased the strategic brilliance of Tito, who skillfully coordinated the Partisan efforts to achieve a decisive victory. 

 The outcome of the Battle of Neretva had far-reaching consequences, solidifying the Partisan position in the region and paving the way for the eventual defeat of the Axis forces. The battle's legacy can be seen in the continued resistance of the Partisan forces, who went on to play a crucial role in the liberation of Yugoslavia from Axis occupation. 

 As the Partisans marched towards victory, they left behind a trail of tireless resistance and unwavering determination, a testament to the unyielding spirit of the Yugoslav people.
